answer.origin: NVIDIA Corporation blog post dated 2026-07-01 (party statement, company publisher) describing a new AI cloud partnership model, with supporting quotes and a Firmus campus forecast; covered company NVDA.

findings.claim: NVIDIA announced a new business model in which AI clouds procure NVIDIA infrastructure for AI-native, enterprise and ISV customers under a revenue-sharing and credit-support model, and NVIDIA earns both standard product revenue and a share of cloud revenue on the supported capacity.
findings.use: Supports the limited conclusion that NVIDIA has publicly announced a model in which it would earn product revenue plus a share of partner cloud revenue on supported capacity, with credit support attached. It does not establish the revenue-share percentage, the scope of supported capacity, or how much NVIDIA's economics depend on partner utilization.
findings.grounds: This is NVIDIA's own description of its announced model, so the company can establish the model's design and announced structure. It is a promotional party statement, not a contract or financial disclosure, so it shows the intended structure rather than realized terms or amounts. The uncertainty that matters for research is whether the revenue-share and credit-support terms are material to NVDA's reported results.
findings.next_check: Look for NVIDIA's 10-Q or 10-K language on revenue-sharing arrangements, cloud partner agreements, and credit support or guarantees, including any disclosed amounts, durations, and accounting treatment.

findings.claim: NVIDIA's model includes credit support for AI clouds, but the article gives no amount, term, counterparty, or conditions for that support.
findings.use: Lead: credit support may create a contingent NVIDIA obligation tied to partner financing, but the existence and size of any guarantee or backstop are unresolved. Keep the weaker supported use that credit support is announced as part of the model.
findings.grounds: The term appears only in NVIDIA's own announcement, which establishes that the model is described as including credit support but does not describe any signed guarantee. The article does not say whether credit support is a guarantee, a financing backstop, or another arrangement, so no contingent-liability size can be inferred from it.
findings.next_check: Check NVIDIA's filings for guarantees, letters of credit, or other off-balance-sheet commitments tied to AI cloud partners, and any disclosed maximum exposure or fair-value treatment.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says the model provides it with a recurring, usage-linked earnings stream from supported AI cloud capacity.
findings.use: Conditional: if partner capacity is highly utilized and generates cloud revenue, NVIDIA's share would recur with usage. The forecast-like characterization does not establish that the stream will be material or recurring over time.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA is describing its own expected economics, so it knows the intended structure but has a promotional incentive. The article itself argues that the capacity must stay highly utilized to support token-scale economics, so the usage-linked stream depends on utilization and partner revenue that are not reported here.
findings.next_check: Track whether NVIDIA reports any revenue line or disclosure tied to cloud revenue shares, and whether partner utilization or revenue data becomes available for supported capacity.

findings.claim: Firmus is building a DSX AI factory campus in Batam, Indonesia, which NVIDIA says is expected to scale to 360 megawatts and up to 170,000 NVIDIA GPUs.
findings.use: Conditional: if the campus is built to the stated scale, it would represent a large potential source of NVIDIA GPU demand through the partner model. The stated figures are a build-out forecast, not a confirmed order or delivery schedule for NVIDIA.
findings.grounds: The figures come from NVIDIA's announcement and are framed as expected scale, so they are forecast rather than observed. Firmus, the builder, is quoted separately in the article, but the article does not give Firmus's own financing, timing, or purchase commitments. The key uncertainty is whether the campus reaches the stated capacity and whether NVIDIA GPUs are procured through this model.
findings.next_check: Check Firmus or Indonesian regulatory and project announcements for financing, power approvals, construction milestones, and any stated GPU purchase schedule or agreement with NVIDIA.

findings.claim: NVIDIA says AI cloud companies are already building DSX AI factories to serve customers and workloads across regions.
findings.use: Lead: this suggests partner build-out activity beyond Firmus, but the article names only Firmus and Sharon AI and gives no sites, sizes or timelines for other partners.
findings.grounds: This is NVIDIA's general characterization of the initiative and is not independently verified in the article. It is useful for identifying further partners to investigate, but it does not establish the number, scale, or status of DSX AI factories.
findings.next_check: Identify other named AI cloud partners building DSX AI factories and check their public project disclosures for scale, financing, and NVIDIA procurement.

findings.claim: Sharon AI's CEO James Manning described the collaboration with NVIDIA as a pivotal moment in Sharon AI's mission to deliver sovereign, large-scale AI compute infrastructure.
findings.use: Usable only for the limited claim that Sharon AI publicly describes a strategic collaboration with NVIDIA on large-scale AI compute infrastructure. It gives no capacity, contract, or revenue detail.
findings.grounds: The speaker is Sharon AI's CEO, so he can speak to his company's stated collaboration. The quote is promotional and was relayed in NVIDIA's release, so it does not independently confirm terms or the scale of the collaboration.
findings.next_check: Check Sharon AI's own filings or announcements for the terms, capacity, timing, and any NVIDIA procurement or revenue-sharing arrangement.

findings.claim: AI natives such as Baseten, Fireworks AI and Together AI show where compute demand is headed, needing access to AI cloud capacity for training, fine-tuning and high-volume agentic inference.
findings.use: Lead: these named AI-native companies may be demand sources for the partner model, but the article does not say they buy NVIDIA capacity through it or on what terms.
findings.grounds: NVIDIA is characterizing a general demand trend and naming companies as examples, not reporting their purchases or contracts. The article does not supply their spending or procurement relationship, so the business link to NVDA's revenue remains unresolved.
findings.next_check: Check whether Baseten, Fireworks AI or Together AI disclose NVIDIA-based capacity purchases, cloud partner relationships or related financing in their own filings or announcements.
